lessons: Start hooks immediately with high-stakes mysteries or visceral contrasts, as shown by the shark video achieving a 1.85 retention rate at 10% by presenting an extreme age claim ('older than the United States').
Avoid redundant repetition in early drops; scripts that repeat phrases within the first 30% (such as the guardrail video repeating 'Instead of impaling your vehicle') trigger steep viewer loss.
Eliminate meta-pauses and filler transition lines like 'Pause and guess...' which directly correlate with early drop-offs around the 50% mark in explanatory segments.
Anchor biological and physical comparisons to familiar, high-contrast visuals early on, evidenced by the tuna vs. cod video outperforming peers with 0.86 relative end retention.
Do not rely solely on countdowns or abstract mechanics without immediate stakes, as low-performing videos show steep drop-offs at the 10% and 50% marks when explanations feel overly academic.
worst_moment_types: Redundant phrasing repeating the exact same concept or line back-to-back
Slow narrative pauses or guessing prompts (e.g., 'Pause and guess...')
Academic or abstract definitions occurring before the viewer understands the physical stakes
Vague transition lines that lack concrete imagery ('They look like similar fruits')
best_hook_types: Extreme comparative statements ('This shark is older than the United States')
Visceral physical paradoxes ('Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back')
Counter-intuitive everyday mysteries ('Why Onions Make You Cry')
